findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzle for the fountain drink machine was observed with encrusted, lumpy brown substances caked into the blades of the nozzle. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. The items was disassembled and moved to dish for cleaning during the inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-201.16(A) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE.

Painters tape was observed being used to hold a light fixture in place in the standing freezer next to the cook line. Tape is not considered a cleanable surface when exposure to moisture and food. This item should be repaired correctly using smooth and easily cleanable materials that do not pose a potential for food contamination.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a Certified FOOD Protection Manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC during the inspection was unable to provide a CFPM certificate for an employee available at the facility during the inspection. They stated that they had taken and passed the test but the tester had a surgery and had not yet given them the certificate. The inspector directed them to servesafe’s website to attempt and get a copy that way. No certification was provided by the end of the inspection. Ensure that there are enough CFPM’s available at the facility to cover all shifts and that they certification is available at the facility at all times.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

A food handler was observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hand to turn off the water faucet. Education was conducted. Ensure that a clean barrier is used to turn off the faucet so that the freshly cleaned hands are not re-contaminated immediately after washing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

A food handler was observed to put on gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted. Ensure that hands are washed when needed per the code, including prior to donning gloves.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

One of the two observed sani buckets showed approximately 100 ppm quat on the inspector’s test strips. Effective concentrations for this chemical are a minimum of 200 ppm. The PIC was shown and remade the bucket to correct.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Sour cream packets in the cold holding well to the right of the prepared sandwich slides are observed with internal temperatures of 60F. The PIC was shown. The container the packets are sitting in is setting out of the well slightly because they are in another well. The second, deeper well appears significantly colder. The current set of packets was discarded to correct the immediate violation and the future ones will be left in the bottom well ONLY to allow for effective cold holding.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

1) The corner covering around the wall next to the mop sink is pulling away and exposing a large gap. 2) The hand sink next to the walk in cooler is observed to have a gap around the junction to the wall. 3) The hand sink next to the fryers has a small gap forming at the right side top junction to the wall. The PIC was shown all three locations and instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection. The PIC stated that they would contact their maintenance person for these repairs.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria at all times. 

Multiple buckets of sanitizer in the facility are observed with low concentrations on the inspector’s test strips. The PIC was unaware of the last time that the buckets had been remade and replaced the buckets during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers used in the facility are maintained at correct concentrations at all times.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Containers of whipped topping and half n’ half are observed at room temperature next to the rack used for storing prepared sandwiches. An internal temperature was taken and showed 71.5 F. All three observed containers had manufacturer labeling indicating the refrigeration is required for these products at all times. The items were discarded during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. The PIC stated that these items were normally stored in the cooler under this location. Ensure that these items are stored correctly in temperature control at all times moving forward.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Multiple food contact single service storage locations around the kitchen are observed with dust and debris in contact with the single service items. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean the locations and to keep the locations cleaned moving forward. Ensure that all single service items are stored in such a way as to be protected from contamination prior to use.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW. 

The drain under the customer service shelving is observed backed up and believed to be clogged. The PIC was shown and instructed to have the drain unclogged prior to the follow up in three days. Ensure that all drains are maintained a state where they remain functional at al times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria at all times. 

The spray bottle of sanitizer next to the three part sink did not register on the inspector’s test strips. The bottle barely registered on that facility test strips. Education was conducted and the bottle remade to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers used in the facility are maintained at correct concentrations at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

Multiple pans on the front sandwich line are observed soiled during this inspection. This line has not been in use today. The PIC was shown and had the pans moved to dish for recleaning. Ensure that all dishes are cleaned completely after use.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

Several locations throughout the facility do not appear to be getting sufficient cleaning. Locations include: 1) along the walls, in corners and around the shelf wheels in the walk in cooler; 2) behind the ice machine and; 3) under/around the drive thru equipment. The PIC was shown and instructed to have the locations cleaned regularly enough to prevent soil accumulation.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

The sinks in the the men’s bathroom and next to the fryers are without paper towels during this inspection. The PIC was notified and replaced the paper towels during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzle of the fountain drink machine in the drive thru area is soiled and in need of cleaning. When asked the PIC indicated that it was soaked in sanitizer nightly as its cleaning procedure. This is not sufficient. This is a direct food contact surface and should be thoroughly cleaned (wash/rinse/sanitize) regularly to maintain clean. Nightly cleaning is suggested. The items was moved to dish and cleaned immediately to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are regularly cleaned so that they are maintained free of contaminants.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. 

Multiple pans in the storage area are observed with food debris still on them. Other items were found freshly washed and with food debris still on them. The PIC was shown and the items moved back to dish for re-cleaning to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all dishes are completely cleaned prior to storage. Education and training for the dish washers was suggested.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.comment:
5-403.12: Condensate drainage and other non-SEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW. 

On arrival the right and front sections of the kitchen are observed with significant amounts of water. Investigation with the PIC indicated that it is coming from floor a drain in the customer seating area. The floor drain is clogged and has the drain from the customer fountain drink machine emptying in it. Because of the clogged floor drain the water mixture is flowing onto the floor and into the kitchen. Per the PIC they have been instructed to suck out the drain as needed. This is not sufficient and a plumber will be needed to fix the drain. A follow up is being set for two weeks. This is believed to be sufficient time for maintenance to be conducted. Until that time the water should be sucked up regularly and the floor mopped consistently to ensure that the fluids are not a concern for contamination of the kitchen.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

Multiple employees are observed to don or change gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted. Ensure that hand washing takes place prior to donning gloves each time.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

On arrival, the hand sink next to the prep line had multiple brooms, dust pans and a trash can in front of it, making it difficult to access/use. The PIC was consulted and the items removed to correct. Ensure that all of the hand sinks are maintained accessible at all times to promote good hand washing practices.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. 

A grey bucket on the counter next to the front hand washing station is observed without a label, and appears to be a cleaner/disinfectant. Discussion with the PIC lead to the belief that it is the bathroom cleaner. The bucket was discarded to correct tthe immediate violation. Ensure that all containers with chemicals in them are labeled moving forward.
